newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks move higher after trade data.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks move higher after trade data.

text.p: Mexican stocks were approaching the 4,700-point milestone at midday Wednesday, recovering from an earlier downturn after the release of stronger-than-expected trade figures, dealers said.
"The figures weren't amazing, but they reassured dealers, as a couple of months ago many were expecting deficits," a floor trader said.
The blue-chip IPC share index was up 41.82 points, or 0.90 percent, at 4,694.01. Trading volume was moderate at 41.3 million shares.
Earlier, the Finance Ministry said Mexico posted a preliminary June trade surplus of $182 million. On average, analysts had forecast a $165 million surplus, according to a Reuters survey.
Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex), which accounted for 14 percent of all shares traded, made the biggest contribution to the market gains, dealers said.
"Telmex is up despite its lukewarm earnings posted last night. It is reacting more on Telebras, which hit us hard last week," the trader added.
Telmex was up 16 centavos to 19.82 pesos, while its Brazilian counterpart, Telecomunicacoes Brasileiras (Telebras) preferred shares gained 2.50 reais to 157.00 reais in Sao Paulo.
Dealers said C shares of retailer Cifra SA were also helping up drive the market. The issue gained 10 centavos to 13.18 amid demand from foreign investors.
On the broad market, gainers outnumbered decliners by 57 to 24, out of a total of 95 stocks that had changed hands.
